evidence.curator_note: First (gamma) hydrogen rearrangement producing the distonic radical-cation intermediate, identical to the rH step of eq 4.45: gamma H (H8, on C2) transfers to the carbonyl oxygen O6, radical to C2, carbonyl becomes protonated-carbonyl oxocarbenium. This first transfer is drawn in the eq-4.45 panel (3 arcs, fully depicted radical-site HAT); moves <1,2,3> encode it. Eq 4.46 itself begins from the resulting distonic ion, drawn in its left panel as the charge-migrated resonance form (charge on the ester O, radical on gamma C, carbonyl drawn as a neutral =O-H); the vertical equilibrium arrow on the page marks that resonance. Within eq 4.46's own figure no arcs are drawn for this first transfer.

Second (delta) hydrogen rearrangement with fragmentation (McLafferty +1 / double H transfer): the delta H (H9, on C1) is delivered to the ester oxygen O4 while the beta C3-O4 bond cleaves, expelling a neutral allyl radical (CH2=CH-CH2., odd electron on Cdelta=C1) and leaving the even-electron protonated carboxylic acid [R'C(OH)2]+ (both oxygens protonated, oxocarbenium on O6). Book draws 2 arcs on the charge-migrated resonance form (eq 4.46, left panel): arc A (delta C-H -> ester O) corresponds to move <3>, arc B (beta C-O bond -> gamma radical carbon) corresponds to move <2>. Moves <1,4,5> are implicit homolysis/pi-forming hooks required for electron balance (not drawn on the page): <1> the gamma radical initiating the C2=C3 pi bond, <4> the delta C1-H9 homolysis leaving the radical on Cdelta, <5> completion of the O4-H9 bond from the second electron of the cleaving C3-O4 bond.

Cross-linked MOD rules (rule_index by_equation 4.46): IMS_4_46_rH_1, IMS_4_46_rH_2, IMS_4_46_rH_2_. IMS_4_46_rH_1 is the first (gamma) transfer but its product [H]1[C]2[C.]3[C]5[O+]6[C]7([C]8){=}[O]9[H]4 encodes the charge-migrated resonance form with a valence-broken oxygen: O9 is written neutral while carrying a C=O double bond AND an O-H bond (3 bonds, should be O+), and the charge sits on the ester O6; my step_rH_first instead uses the chemically valid oxocarbenium resonance form drawn in eq 4.45. IMS_4_46_rH_2 [H]1[C]2[C.]3[C]4[O]5[C]6([C]7){=}[O]8[H]9>>[C]2[C.]3[C]4.[H]1[O+]5{=}[C]6([C]7)[O]8[H]9 matches step_rH_second in substance (second H to the ester O, C-O cleavage, protonated-acid oxocarbenium + a 3-carbon neutral radical) but leaves the neutral fragment without its allyl C=C double bond (radical shown static on the gamma carbon). MISMATCH on IMS_4_46_rH_2_: its product [C]2[C.]3[C]4.[H]1[O+]5[C]6([C]7){=}[O+]8[H]9 carries TWO formal positive charges (O5+ and O8+) on the protonated-acid fragment (product charge +2 vs reactant +1) -- not charge-balanced; it is the second resonance form of the protonated acid (the two forms are drawn at the bottom-right of the page) but the charge is double-counted.

Generic scheme (R, R'): the book prints no m/z and no intensity for 4.46. m/z 61.0284 is RDKit-computed monoisotopic mass for the protonated acetic acid (even-electron [CH3C(OH)2]+) from the chosen concrete instantiation R=CH3, R'=CH3 (propyl acetate, M+. = 102.0675); it is not a measured value. Neutral co-product is the allyl radical (41.0391). This McLafferty +1 ion is one mass unit above the single-transfer acid radical cation of eq 4.45 (60.0206).
